newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TWI weakness brings bears out in NZ bill market.
newsitem.headline: TWI weakness brings bears out in NZ bill market.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 93.21 (PREV 93.23) 90-DAYS 6.88 (PREV 6.89)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.50 PCT (PREV 6.50) US 5-YR 6.29 (PREV 6.34)
NZ MCI -0.90 (PREV -0.82)
* Weakness in TWI brings out bank bill bears
* Bonds picked to trade in range ahead of budget and MPS
* Foreign debt down on expectations but fails to excite
New Zealand bank bills surrendered morning gains by Monday's close as the market responded to weakness in the Trade-Weighted Index.
That was largely the result of U.S. dollar weakness against the yen and dealers said that the volatile dollar holds the key to direction of the New Zealand short end.
They expect further choppy trading in the dollar in the lead-up to the G-7 meeting in Denver at the end of the week.
Weakness in the TWI translated into the Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) moving to over 90 basis points looser in interest rate terms than the Reserve Bank's desired conditions.
The long bonds ended five basis points lower than Friday's close at 7.07 percent although they gave up a few of their gains as the early morning buying ran into solid selling.

Dealers expect the bonds to range-trade in a transaction-driven market ahead of next week's budget and Reserve Bank Monetary Policy Statement with strong resistance experienced just below 7.0 percent.
The shorter bonds are seen most vulnerable to any pre-budget/MPS rally.
Data showed New Zealand total overseas debt at $75.5 billion at March 31, well below the $79.8 billion forecast by economists, but it moved the market not one whit.
-- Simon Louisson, Wellington newsroom, 64 4 4734 746
